chapters.title: Content Access Control
chapters.subtitle: Let only the right roles view an item

steps.text: Some content is meant for one team only. This video shows how Content Access Control limits who can view a content item to the roles you pick on that item: why it exists, how to set it up on a content type, how to restrict an item, and how to check the result.

chapters.title: Why restrict content by role
chapters.subtitle: One page for everyone, another for one team

steps.text: Some pages are not for everyone: a supervisor handbook, an internal price list, or notes for a single department.
Permissions normally apply to a whole content type, so two pages of the same type are open to the same people.
Content Access Control lets the editor choose, on each item, the roles that may view it.
Everyone else is refused that item, and the rest of the site stays open as before.

chapters.title: How it works
chapters.subtitle: The Role Picker part and one setting

steps.text: It builds on the Role Picker part, which lets an editor pick one or more roles on a content item.
On the content type, one setting, Restrict content, turns the picker into an access rule.
A person can view an item only if they hold at least one of the picked roles. An item with no roles picked stays open to everyone.
Only viewing is limited. Who can edit, publish or delete the item still follows the usual permissions, and administrators can always view every item.

chapters.title: Set up a content type
chapters.subtitle: Add the Role Picker and restrict content

steps.text: Open Design, Content Definition, Content Types, and edit the type that needs restricted items. Here it is Handbook Page.
Click Add Parts. Role Picker is in the list, described as allowing you to select one or more roles. Click Add and Configure.
The Display Name is what editors see above the picker. Give it a clear name, such as Limit access to selected roles.

Exclude roles hides the roles that should never be picked, such as Anonymous and Authenticated. Required means an editor must pick a role. Allow multiple lets an editor pick more than one, and the Hint is help text under the picker.
Restrict content turns the picker into an access rule: only people in the selected roles can view the item. Tick it, and save.

chapters.title: Restrict an item
chapters.subtitle: Pick the roles that may view it

steps.text: Open Content, Content Items, and create a new Handbook Page.
Give the page a title, such as Supervisor handbook, and type its text. The role picker is below the text.
The picker shows the hint, and lists the roles of the site. Search for a role, and tick the ones that may view this page. Here it is Supervisor.
Publish the page. From now on, only people who hold the Supervisor role can view it.
To lift the restriction from one page, untick all its roles and save. To lift it from every page of the type, untick Restrict content on the part.

chapters.title: Check the result
chapters.subtitle: Sign in as someone with, and without, the role

steps.text: Always check the result by signing in as other people. Casey Morgan holds the Support Agent role. The Support hours page has no roles picked, so Casey can open it.
The Supervisor handbook is restricted to the Supervisor role. Casey does not hold it, so the page is refused.
Jordan Lee holds the Supervisor role, so the same address opens the handbook.

chapters.title: What to use it for
chapters.subtitle: Four pages that are not for everyone

steps.text: A supervisor handbook or an escalation guide that only supervisors should read.
An internal price list or discount rules for the sales team.
Documents for one partner or one department, each limited to its own role.
Announcements and procedures for a single team.

Set up the Role Picker once on a content type, and turn on Restrict content. Then every page of that type can have its own audience: pick the roles on an item, and only people who hold one of them can view it. Thanks for watching.
